sections.title: The Numbers, And The Date They Were True
sections.content:
Reviews lifted over the night of 25-26 October 2026, three days before the 29 October release. As of 26 October 2026:

  • Metacritic: 88 on PC (31-33 critic reviews as the page fills in) and 87 on PS5 (a smaller day-one sample)
  • OpenCritic: 91 across 22-24 reviews, rated Mighty, with 100% of critics recommending it and a place in the site's 100th percentile
  • 30 positive, 1 mixed, 0 negative on Metacritic - 97% positive

Quote these with this date. Day-one averages are rolling: outlets that review later, and outlets Metacritic adds index, will move the number over the next week. The PC and PS5 Metascores are separate samples, and OpenCritic aggregates the game rather than splitting platforms, so 88 and 91 are not competing claims - they answer different questions with different sets of writers. Do not let anyone tell you one number is the real one.

Polygon's framing is the useful headline: an 88 makes this the best-reviewed action game of 2026 so far, ahead of Control Resonant, 007 First Light and Saros, while trailing the year's racing releases (Star Wars Galactic Racer on 88, Forza Horizon 6 on 90).

sections.title: What Players Say, Two Weeks After Launch
sections.content:
Critic scores were fixed before release. The player number was not, and it has moved more than any critic aggregate will: Steam's user score sat at about 77% ("Mostly Positive") in the first hours of 29 October, reached roughly 90% by 2 November, and stood at 94% across more than 100,000 reviews ("Very Positive") on 12 November. The same day the game was 7th on Steam's global top-sellers list and 2nd in China.

Read the shape of that curve carefully. The early reviews were dominated by shader compilation stalls and start-up crashes on PC, which patch 1.0302256 addressed on 4 November. But a rising score is also the ordinary arithmetic of a 30-40 hour game: players who quit in the first hour review on day one, and players who finish arrive a week later. Both effects point the same way, and no source separates them - so the honest statement is that the score improved, not that patching caused all of it.

What players consistently praise matches what critics praised: the combat, the weapon switching, the boss encounters and the art direction. What players consistently complain about now that the game is out:

  • Difficulty spikes on optional bosses. Hua, Deadly Betrothed was the flashpoint and the reason S-GAME nerfed her grabs - but only on Wayfarer and Pathbreaker. Players who beat her before 4 November on those settings did so against the harder version.
  • Repetitive ordinary enemies. The same criticism Eurogamer raised in its 6/10, and the one that survived launch intact.
  • Missing quality-of-life features. Photo mode and a boss-rush mode were the two most-requested additions in replies to the sales announcement. S-GAME has not confirmed either.
  • No DLC or roadmap. The 2 November announcement addressed bug fixes only. The director has said the team has ideas for sequels, expansions, animation and film, but also that the first game's result would decide what gets made - a result now in hand, and still no announcement.

The award result belongs here rather than in the critic section: at the Golden Joystick Awards on 11 November the game finished second in Ultimate Game of the Year with 16%, one point behind Resident Evil: Requiem. Voting closed on 30 October, one day after release, so that vote measured anticipation more than the shipped game.

sections.title: Every Published Score We Can Attribute
sections.content:
Sorted high to low. Platform is listed where the outlet or aggregator said so; "not stated" means the review did not specify, which is common and worth knowing when you read a performance verdict.

  • 100 / 10 - PCGamesN. "A stunning action RPG that gives the best of all time a run for their money... an intricately designed Metroidvania at heart."
  • 100 / 10 - But Why Tho?. Calls it both a game-of-the-year candidate and a gateway to wuxia for new audiences.
  • 10 / 10 - The Outerhaven. "A generational game", and explicitly: "Soulslike fans should give it a shot too, even though it clearly isn't one."
  • 100 - SteamDeckHQ. "The best game I have played this year" - a handheld-relevant verdict, since the install is around 135 GB.
  • 100 - Wccftech. Compares the feeling to Elden Ring and Street Fighter 6.
  • 100 - Saudi Gamer. Notes a few issues that "barely affect an otherwise outstanding experience".
  • 98 - screenactu. "Phantom Blade Zero's combat system should be taught in every game design school"; praises exploration, faults the lock-on system.
  • 95 - Combo Infinito. Cites a 55-hour run; faults level design, narrative and PC performance.
  • 95 - Areajugones. Praises traversal and boss invention; faults scattered storytelling and missing map markers.
  • 90 / 9 - IGN (Travis Northup, 50 hours). Best combat in years, story "plays it extremely safe", invisible barriers and technical hiccups.
  • 90 - Gameliner. Praises audio, soundtrack and voice acting; faults fairly linear levels and limited exploration.
  • 9 - GamesRadar, 9 - Screen Rant, 9 - Retcon, 9.0 - One More Game. Screen Rant's split is revealing: visuals 10, audio 10, story 7, gameplay 7.
  • 9.5 / 10 - SavePoint Gaming (PS5 Pro). The highest score we have seen on PlayStation hardware; flags camera issues and familiar side-quest objectives.
  • 8.5 / 10 - GAMES.CH (85 on Metacritic). Praises the reduced reliance on farming; faults linear environments and overlong text passages.
  • 8 / 10 - GameSpot (Richard Wakeling). Headline: "Combat Is So Good, You Won't Care The Story Makes No Sense".
  • 4 / 5 - VGC (Dave Aubrey). "Undoubtedly stronger than genre stablemates like Black Myth: Wukong", but calls the narrative and characters "bland" and the levels too linear.
  • 8 / 10 - Checkpoint Gaming (PS5, Omi Koulas). Wanted more from Soul himself: "another stoic, masculine warrior" beside more interesting NPCs.
  • 7 / 10 - Creative Bloq. Several "annoying design decisions" stop it being great.
  • 6 / 10 - Eurogamer (3/5, Emma Kent). The low outlier and the only mixed review: fluid cinematic kung fu combat, but balance and quality issues "dim its shine", with boss fights feeling like "waiting your turn to get hits in with a wooden sword".

Platform tested is stated for SavePoint (PS5 Pro), Checkpoint Gaming (PS5) and Screen Rant's PC verdict; the rest were not specified in what we read.

sections.title: What The Critics Agree On
sections.content:
Unanimous, and it is what you would expect: the combat. Even the 6/10 review calls the kung fu combat wonderfully fluid and cinematic. The specific things writers keep returning to are parry timing, the variety of weapons and what they do to the moveset, and the boss fights. Screen Rant's story 7 / gameplay 7 split is the most compressed honest summary available: this is a game whose presentation is scored far above its writing.

The repeated criticisms, roughly in order of how often they appear:

  • Story and characters. GameSpot, VGC, Polygon, Checkpoint, GamingBible, screenactu (scattered storytelling) and Combo Infinito all land here. This is the single most common reason a score dropped.
  • Repetitive ordinary enemies. GameSpot says mowing down dozens of weak foes gets tiring and hides the real depth; the pre-embargo leak made the same point about cleared locations feeling empty.
  • Linearity. Gameliner, GAMES.CH and VGC all flag limited exploration and linear levels - worth knowing if the soulslike comparison is why you are interested; the reviews say the structure is more guided than that implies, while screenactu and Areajugones found exploration a genuine surprise.
  • Technical finish. IGN on invisible barriers and hiccups, Combo Infinito on PC performance, Game*Spark on unstable actions, SavePoint on the camera.
  • Combat pacing at boss level. Eurogamer's complaint is the one substantive design criticism in the set: small-scale fights feel creative and expressive, boss fights feel like taking turns.
  • Quality-of-life gaps. Lock-on (screenactu), no map markers (Areajugones), overlong text (GAMES.CH), no controller remapping in the reviewed build.

sections.title: Performance: What Is Actually Established
sections.content:
Very little, and this is the part of the review wave most likely to be misreported. What we have:

  • Screen Rant says PC performance "barely ever skips a frame" - one reviewer's rig, with no hardware specs or frame-time capture published alongside it.
  • Combo Infinito lists PC performance among its reasons the game is not perfect.
  • Critical Hits, in the review that leaked before the embargo, described smooth visuals in Balanced mode on a base PS5.
  • Previews through October had raised unstable frame rates in heavy combat; the studio's own delay to 29 October was justified partly on visual polish.

A game built around frame-precise parries deserves measured frame-pacing data, and none of it exists yet. Until Digital Foundry-style breakdowns land, treat both "it runs great" and "it stutters" as single-system reports. The concrete requirements are on PC requirements, including the Denuvo caveat, and the install size on release date and unlock times.

sections.title: How The Embargo Actually Went
sections.content:
Worth recording, because it is a rare case where a leak can be checked against what happened:

  1. No official date or hour was ever published. S-GAME did not announce an embargo lift on its site, on X, or on the Steam or PlayStation Store pages.
  2. 20 October: TwistedVoxel and Playfront reported a lift on 26 October. The date traced back to a ResetEra thread, relayed through r/GamingLeaksAndRumours under that subreddit's "Grain of Salt" tag.
  3. 25-26 October: reviews went out - Metacritic timestamps individual reviews to 25 October 2026, which in US time zones is the evening before the 26 October date the leak named, and the same moment in Asian time zones.
  4. One outlet broke it entirely: Brazilian site Critical Hits uploaded a full 8.5/10 review before the lift and deleted it, which notebookcheck and vgtimes both covered.

So the leaked date was effectively right, and the three-days-before-release window is earlier than the usual one-or-two-days pattern. Eurogamer additionally said embargo restrictions stopped it discussing some of the story - which is why the lowest score in the set is also the least spoilery.

sections.title: Should You Buy It, According To The Reviews
sections.content:
Reading the set as a purchase decision rather than a score:

  • If you want a combat game - every review in the set, including the 6/10, says the fighting is exceptional. That is close to a unique position: no other 2026 action release has critics agreeing on the mechanics this strongly while disagreeing about the writing.
  • If you want a story - do not buy it for that. The single most common reason scores dropped was narrative, and GameSpot put it in the headline.
  • If you want 60+ hours of content - reviewers report 50 to 55 hours on a first playthrough; see how long to beat for the breakdown.
  • If you are on PC and worried about performance - wait for measured benchmarks rather than this page; the verdicts currently rest on individual rigs.
  • If you wanted a disc - still no launch-day disc. The reviews changed nothing about that; see physical edition and collector's edition.

sections.title: Sources And How This Page Is Maintained
sections.content:
Read 26 October 2026: Metacritic critic reviews, OpenCritic, Polygon's roundup, Shane the Gamer, notebookcheck on the embargo leak, and Game*Spark. Scores and quotations belong to the outlets named.

This page was written on 22 October as a "no scores yet" page; it was rewritten on 26 October when the embargo lifted. We will keep the aggregates current to the day and add outlets as they publish. We do not average the averages ourselves, and we do not carry a score we cannot attribute to a named critic.
